title: daybook-batch-summary-dara
content:
Purpose: quick personal sheet to capture short runs and immediate heuristics for batching/quantization tradeoffs. Not a canonical lab doc — lightweight, chaotic, meant for quick iteration and TODOs.

Top-level takeaway (so far): for our 7B family, batch sizes between 6–12 hit best cost/latency sweet spot at seq<=512 on A100-40. Quantized int8 reduces p50 by ~10–15% on CPU-bound pieces but watch for quality regressions on long-tail prompts.

Run CSV (most recent first):
Run,Date,Model,Variant,SeqLen,Batch,Req/s,AvgLat_ms,P95_ms,Tokens/req,Cost_per_1k_tokens,Result,Notes
R-211,2025-11-01,redwood-7b,fp16,256,8,140,34,78,420,0.75,ok,"steady, no mem spikes; try batch=10 next"
R-204,2025-10-29,redwood-7b,int8,256,12,160,30,68,420,0.48,good,"int8: lower cost, small quality drift on adversarial prompts (see sample IDs A12-A15)"
R-199,2025-10-24,redwood-7b,fp16,512,6,90,56,110,820,0.85,slow,"seq512 increases KV pressure; consider prefix cache for warm repeated prompts"
R-187,2025-10-10,redwood-3b,int8,256,16,210,22,50,410,0.34,excellent,"3B + int8 seems very cost-effective; baseline for cheap inner-loop tasks"
R-150,2025-09-21,redwood-13b,fp16,128,4,60,48,112,220,1.6,expensive,"13B is overkill for short seq tasks; reserve for quality-critical routes"

Quick micro-analyses:
- Cost calc shorthand: cost_per_1k_tokens reported is run-level estimate (infra cost + token billing proxies). Err +/-10%.
- Latency pattern: avg grows nonlinearly with seqlen after ~300 due to KV resizing and attention kernels. P95 spikes correlate with GC on host (investigate host-side alloc patterns).
- Batching impact: doubling batch from 8->16 improves tokens/sec but increases p95 by 40–60ms on tail; user-facing SMS-like apps prefer p95 so cap batch at 8–12.

Notes to self / TODOs: 
- [ ] Run dd-trace on R-199 type runs to capture host alloc timeline (ask SRE for brief instr).
- [ ] Sweep batch=10 for redwood-7b,int8 at seq=256 (compare quality using prompt-set-eval-3).
- [ ] Add a small eval harness that flags perplexity > +3% vs fp16 baseline for candidate quant configs.
- [ ] Consolidate sample failures (A12-A15) into a single gist and link to PR.

Open questions:
- Is the cost-per-1k stable across zones? I saw 6% uplift in eu-west-1 for same config on 2025-10-30 — network/storage difference? track with same image+AMI.
- When is it acceptable to fallback to 3B for degraded quality routes? Define heuristic based on expected utility not just latency.

Mini checklist before promoting config:
- perf: stable p50/p95 across 10 runs
- quality: eval-set delta <= 2% for key metrics
- infra: no host OOMs, <=2% transient errors
- rollout plan: canary at 5% traffic for 24h with auto-fallback

Reference snippets (for quick copy):
- common command to run micro-bench (local): 
  ./bench_local --model redwood-7b --variant int8 --batch 12 --seq 256 --runs 50 --out r-XXX.json

- quick note to Rajiv: "If int8 fails on A12-A15, re-run with per-channel calibration (try 64 calibration steps) and compare logits distribution."

Pinned samples to inspect (local IDs):
- A12: long-tail conversational with code block -> bad tokenization tokens 45-52
- A14: instruction-contradiction -> hallucination at step 32

Evening log (freeform):
- felt like experiments were noisy today; probably from concurrent dedicated pool maintenance. Keep this sheet as quick log, push cleaned tables to shared_drive/engineering/applied-ml when stable.

Change history (local):
- 2025-09-21: created initial template and baseline runs R-150
- 2025-10-10: added 3B experiments and started int8 trials
- 2025-10-24..11-01: tightened batch sweep and recorded R-199..R-211

End.
